A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SubspaceAD and contain readable main text and Appendices A–G. Their equations, tables, figures, and corresponding experiments support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original SubspaceAD benchmark results, ablations, qualitative evaluations, and latency measurements on MVTec-AD and VisA.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical evaluations and revises numerous reported results.

M1.justification: The frozen DINOv2 feature extraction, layer averaging, PCA fitting, reconstruction-residual scoring, TVaR aggregation, and localization procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MVTec-AD and VisA under the same few-shot, batched zero-shot, and full-shot scenarios. The rotation-agnostic Transistor evaluation also appears in both.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the few-shot, zero-shot, full-shot, qualitative, and latency comparisons. Revised rankings do not introduce or remove comparison methods.

E3.justification: The stated metrics, sampling, resolutions, augmentations, backbone configurations, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Revised scores do not establish an actual protocol change; no setting revision is documented.

E4.justification: The existing resolution, aggregation, backbone, PCA-threshold, and rotation analyses retain their questions but revise quantitative evidence. For example, Appendix G's one-shot Transistor PRO penalty from rotation increases from 3.8 to 6.3 percentage points. No new analysis or failure-case collection is added.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five independent random-seed runs and report means and standard deviations for the same experiments. Changes to individual standard deviations do not change the reporting practice.

E6.justification: Revisions to central quantitative evidence reverse important comparative rankings. In Table 1, four-shot VisA PRO changes from 93.8 to 96.0, overtaking unchanged AnomalyDINO at 94.1. In Table 8, full-shot VisA PRO changes from 94.9 to 96.9, overtaking AnomalyDINO at 96.1. One-shot VisA image AUROC decreases from 93.4 to 93.2. Ablation, per-category, DINOv3, and rotation results also change; batched zero-shot and latency results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, PCA assumptions and probabilistic interpretation, scoring equations, and complexity analysis are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same training-free PCA/DINOv2 contribution and general state-of-the-art few-shot claim. The abstract's revised VisA AUROC changes a reported result rather than the contribution's scope.

C2.justification: Appendix B qualifies DINOv3's inferiority as an overall DINOv2 advantage, especially for localization. Appendix C replaces the previous performance-versus-memory-cost discussion with superiority across all reported VisA metrics without memory banks. Mechanism explanations and substantive failure limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, latency information, and code/demo access remain unchanged. The approximately 300 ms inference statement removed from Appendix C remains available in Section 3.5.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are unchanged. The work retains its positioning of PCA-based normality modeling relative to reconstruction, memory-bank, and vision-language approaches.

P1.justification: Localized rewriting updates Section 4.5 and Appendices A–C and G, including clearer percentage-point language. The section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 4 and 5 are redrawn with revised axes and legends, and Figure 5 moves below the backbone discussion. Figure 4's dataset line styles now agree with its caption. Other figures and table structures are largely retained.

improvement.justification: Clearer wording and corrected Figure 4 labels provide limited benefits, but v3 introduces unexplained disagreement between default ablation rows and the main results. For example, four-shot VisA image AUROC was 94.7 in Tables 1, 3, and 4 in v2; v3 retains 94.7 in Table 1 but reports 94.1 in Tables 3 and 4, without stating a setting difference. The PDFs do not resolve this discrepancy or explain the broader score revisions, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
